title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: Player Two's sole placed unit is the hero SALADIN, a Kurdish-Ayyubid sultan who died in 1193 — 336 years before 1529 and from the wrong dynasty entirely; the engine offers no Suleiman hero but does offer generic Turkish gunpowder troops and at minimum a non-named commander, so a named 12th-century hero was avoidable.

The garrison is armed with MAN_AT_ARMS and CROSSBOWMAN, i.e. 13th-14th century melee infantry and crossbows, while the brief promises Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers — AoE2 provides both the LANDSKNECHT and the HAND_CANNONEER, so this mismatch is avoidable.
A generic KING unit stands in for Niklas Graf Salm, a professional soldier and not a monarch; no Habsburg/Imperial commander figure is otherwise represented.

No Ottoman material culture is placed at all — no Janissaries (available in the engine), no bombard cannon or siege camp, no Ottoman-side buildings; the besieging army exists only as trigger spawns of unspecified type.

GUARD_TOWER x8 and a CASTLE represent Vienna's defences, but Vienna in 1529 was notoriously defended by an outdated single medieval curtain wall hastily earth-backed — the fortified castle-and-towers layout overstates the defences.
3083 oak trees blanket a 144x144 map for a scenario set in a densely built walled city surrounded by cleared glacis and suburbs the defenders had burned down before the siege.

issues_found: The Ottoman commander is the hero SALADIN — a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan — standing in for Suleiman the Magnificent (1529). The engine ships no Suleiman hero, so a renamed generic elite unit (e.g. a Janissary or Elite Mameluke) was the correct choice; using a different named historical figure is avoidable error.
The garrison contains no Landsknechts despite the brief naming them; the engine offers the Teutonic Landsknecht explicitly. Instead the defence is MAN_AT_ARMS x8 and CROSSBOWMAN x7.
No Spanish arquebusiers: the engine's Hand Cannoneer (and Spanish Conquistador) exist and would represent 1529 firearms; crossbowmen misdate the garrison's weaponry by a century.
Player 1's commander is a bare KING object rather than a renamed hero/unit for Niklas Graf Salm, so the dialogue's 'Commander Salm' has no on-map referent.
Both players' civilizations are RANDOM — architecture set, and thus whether Vienna looks Central European or e.g. Meso-American, is left to chance, and the Ottoman side is not assigned Turks.
3,083 oak trees on a 144x144 map make the setting a forest, not the Danube plain and suburbs before a walled imperial city; no river, no Ottoman siege camp/trench works are represented.
The brief's central mechanic — countermining the Ottoman sappers, the actual decisive fighting at Vienna — is entirely absent; there is no mining/countermining representation of any kind.

The siege is compressed to a 10-minute 'survive until dawn' with four assault waves; the historical siege ran roughly three weeks and ended with a general assault on 14 October followed by withdrawal, so 'until dawn' misframes the timescale and the cause of relief.

Only one Ottoman object is actually placed (the Saladin hero); the entire besieging host exists solely as trigger-spawned CREATE_OBJECT calls of unspecified type, so no Janissary/Ottoman force composition is verifiable on the map.

The Ottoman besieger is represented by the hero SALADIN, a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan, standing in for Suleiman the Magnificent (1529) — a ~350-year era error that was avoidable, since a renamed generic unit or a Janissary/Turkish elite would have served

Player 2's roster contains literally nothing but the Saladin hero; the entire Ottoman host exists only as unspecified CREATE_OBJECT spawns, so the janissaries, sipahi cavalry and sapper/artillery train central to the brief are not authored as placed content

Both civilizations are left RANDOM, so Viennese/Central European architecture and the Ottoman opponent's building set and unit access are unassigned — the one setting choice the editor makes trivially available is skipped
The garrison is Man-at-Arms and Crossbowmen: no gunpowder units at all, despite the brief's 'Spanish arquebusiers', and Two-Handed Swordsmen/Champions (the natural Landsknecht stand-in) are absent

Niklas Graf Salm is represented by the KING unit rather than a renamed infantry hero, making the defending commander a non-combatant piece rather than the fighting officer who was mortally wounded on the walls
Map is 3,083 oak trees with forage bushes, sheep and gold/stone mines — a wilderness clearing, not the Danube bank and glacis-cleared suburbs of Vienna
The historically decisive countermining war beneath the Carinthian Gate is only mentioned in the brief and never mechanically or spatially represented
The 'hold until dawn (10:00)' framing recasts a three-week siege broken by autumn rain and supply failure as a single night's defence
The 'VC Eliminate' path lets the player win by wiping the besieging army off the map, which the Vienna garrison never attempted and could not have done
